DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Four Hands, One Jaguar

STS-HS9-L3-10001300-HSVPA910-TRT-LAT-01 • HS Theatre Grades 9–10 • Collaborative Roles in a Theatre Work
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
A play is never one person's work. The actor, the director, the playwright, and the designer each change what the audience sees, and none of them can do the show alone. After every preview night, Marisol's team writes down what people talked about on the way out, and the tally shows which choices are landing. Their jaguar puppet borrows its bright patterns from alebrijes, the carved animals from Oaxaca that no two artists ever paint the same way.
The board says the audience noticed all four jobs about the same. Pick one job and explain what the show would lose if that person quit tomorrow.
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Nayeli doing?
Look at the picture. Say what Nayeli is doing and why it matters for the show. Speak in two complete sentences.
2
What is Esteban holding?
Look at the picture. Say what Esteban is holding and why he needs it. Speak in two complete sentences.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Say what the teacher is doing and why the show needs it. Speak in two complete sentences.
4
Where are these students? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Say what kind of place this is and how you know. Speak in two complete sentences.
5
Tell me about the board.
Look at the picture. Say what the board shows and what the team uses it for. Speak in two complete sentences.
6
What is Marisol wearing?
Look at the picture. Say what Marisol is wearing and what she is doing. Speak in two complete sentences.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CA VAPA Theatre TH:Cr2a (Grades 9–10) — investigate the collaborative nature of the actor, director, playwright, and designers and explore their interdependent roles in a drama or theatre work.
